introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2020. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Questions ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

(Sections: A Map Work, B Physical Geography, C Human Geography, D Cameroon Geography. Question 1 is the only question of Section A.)

Question 4(b) : les coordonnées sont données à titre indicatif (zones étendues) ; le sujet attend un repérage sur le fond de carte, non reproductible dans le JSON.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) (i) Classify the following terms or phrases in an agricultural system under **inputs, processes, and output**, using a table:

**Building of paddocks, young animals, beef, skin, marketing, lush vegetation, planting of fodder, animal dung, suitable climate, sowing of seeds**

(5 marks)

(ii) State **TWO** ways by which human activities bring about global warming.

(2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** In an agricultural system, the **inputs** are what is put into the farm, the **processes** are the activities carried out on the farm, and the **outputs** are what the farm produces.

| Inputs | Processes | Outputs |
|---|---|---|
| Young animals | Building of paddocks | Beef |
| Lush vegetation | Planting of fodder | Skin (hides) |
| Suitable climate | Sowing of seeds | Animal dung |
| | Marketing | |

(Animal dung is a by-product of the animals; it can also be returned to the soil as manure.)

**(ii) Two ways by which human activities bring about global warming.**

1. **Burning fossil fuels** (coal, oil, gas) in factories, power stations and vehicles releases carbon dioxide, the main greenhouse gas.
2. **Deforestation and bush burning:** the felling and burning of forests release carbon dioxide and remove the trees that absorb it.

(Also accepted: methane from cattle and rice fields, and gases such as CFCs from refrigerators and industry.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) On the outline map of the world provided, **locate** and **name** the following:

(i) an area in the temperate lands where forestry is important.

(ii) **TWO** important fishing grounds in the northern hemisphere.

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_4_fig_1.png)

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
To locate an area on an outline map, **shade or mark it** (with a cross or a line) and **write its name** beside it with a pointing line. Use the latitude and longitude scale on the frame of the map (the equator is marked 0 on the sides and the Greenwich meridian 0 on the top and bottom).

**(i) Area in temperate lands where forestry is important (name one).**

- **Canada**, especially the Pacific coast (British Columbia), at about 50 to 58 degrees N and 120 to 130 degrees W, with the coniferous forests; or
- **Scandinavia** (Sweden and Finland), at about 60 to 65 degrees N and 10 to 30 degrees E; or **Russia (Siberia)** in the north.

**(ii) Two important fishing grounds of the northern hemisphere (name two).**

- The **North Sea** (north-west Europe, about 52 to 60 degrees N and 0 to 8 degrees E).
- The **Grand Banks** (off Newfoundland, in the north-west Atlantic, about 44 to 48 degrees N and 50 to 55 degrees W).
- The **north-west Pacific** (off Japan and the Kamchatka coast, about 35 to 55 degrees N and 140 to 165 degrees E).

Marking: 3 marks for the forestry area (location and name) and 3 marks for the two fishing grounds.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) (i) Outline **THREE** ways by which the government of a country can encourage the development of tourism.

(3 marks)

(ii) State **FOUR** reasons for the creation of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).

(4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Three ways by which a government can encourage tourism.**

1. **Building and improving infrastructure:** roads, airports, hotels, electricity and water supply, so that tourists can reach and stay at the tourist sites.
2. **Advertising and promotion:** brochures, websites, tourist offices abroad, participation in international tourism fairs and the organising of festivals.
3. **Protecting the attractions and encouraging investment:** creating national parks, game reserves and museums, training hotel and guide staff, and giving tax advantages to investors. Peace and security for visitors are also essential.

**(ii) Four reasons for the creation of ECOWAS** (created in 1975 by the Treaty of Lagos):

1. To promote **economic integration** and cooperation among the West African countries.
2. To create a **larger market** and increase **trade** between members by removing tariffs and other barriers, and by allowing the free movement of goods, people and capital.
3. To reduce the **dependence** of the member states on outside countries and on a few export products, and to make industrialisation possible by pooling resources.
4. To **develop infrastructure** (roads, telecommunications, energy) jointly and to promote **peace, stability and security** in the region.
